After you do so, the support team will reach out and offer you the option of also increasing the other two quotas.\\n\\n **Note:**\\n\\n Due to overwhelming demand, priority will be given to customers who generate traffic that consumes their existing quota allocation. Your request might be denied if you don't meet this condition.\\n\\nFor `bedrock-mantle` quota increases, see Requesting a quota increase\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-runtime.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources?\",\"context\":\"### Request a quota increase\\n\\nNew AWS accounts might have lower initial quotas than the default quotas. Specific models have non-adjustable fixed quotas. If your workload traffic exceeds your account's on-demand quotas, then contact [AWS Support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/case-management.html#creating-a-support-case) or your account manager to [request a quota increase](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-increase.html). Availability varies by model and AWS Region. Check the model's detail page for Reserved Tier support and the Provisioned Throughput support table for availability. To access Reserved Tier, contact your AWS account team.\\n* Request for quota increase by contacting your account manager or AWS Support if your workload traffic exceeds your account quotas\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-api-error-codes.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"bedrockruntime\",\"context\":\"## type ThrottlingException \\n\\n```\\ntype ThrottlingException struct {\\n RespMetadata protocol.ResponseMetadata `json:\\\"-\\\" xml:\\\"-\\\"`\\n\\n Message_ *string `locationName:\\\"message\\\" type:\\\"string\\\"`\\n // contains filtered or unexported fields\\n}\\n```\\n\\nYour request was throttled because of service-wide limitations. Resubmit\\nyour request later or in a different region. You can also purchase Provisioned\\nThroughput (<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prov-throughput.html>)\\nto increase the rate or number of tokens you can process\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/bedrockruntime/index.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\",\"context\":\"## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. If admitting the request would exceed the quota, the request is throttled with an HTTP 429 response.\\n2. **Output tokens per minute** \u2013 As the model streams or generates output, output tokens are counted against the output-tokens-per-minute quota for that model. If the quota is reached during generation, generation stops and the response is returned with a finish reason indicating the cutoff.\\n\\nAfter the response completes, any unused portion of the initial input-token reservation (the difference between `max_tokens` and the actual output) is replenished to your quota.\\n\\nThe endpoint may apply additional internal rate limiting that is not exposed in Service Quotas. Use retry logic with exponential backoff to handle transient throttling.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint's TPM quotas count input and output tokens together against a single per-model quota, while the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint applies separate input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas. If you run workloads on both endpoints, plan capacity for each endpoint independently. For details on the runtime endpoint's quotas, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search AWS docs for Bedrock quota increase guidance"}

{"id": "e90798f3-3288-4bc3-bca4-1a6ae878f045", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how to raise the quota. Your account's quota list came back empty in us-east-1, so I'm not sure which model or Region is being throttled.

**1. Find the quota that's throttling you**
- Throttling is per model and per Region. It's measured in tokens per minute (TPM) and requests per minute (RPM).
- In Service Quotas, open Amazon Bedrock and look for "On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute for `<model>`". If you call through a cross-Region inference profile, the relevant quota is "Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `<model>`".
- Check the **Adjustable** column. Some model quotas are fixed and can't be raised.
- Don't request an increase for a model marked Legacy or Deprecated. Those requests aren't granted, so migrate to the successor model instead.

**2. Request the increase**
- If the quota is adjustable, request the increase in Service Quotas.
- For the cross-Region TPM quota, request an increase on "Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `<model>`". Support will then offer to raise the on-demand TPM and Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day quotas at the same time.
- If it isn't adjustable, open an AWS Support case or contact your account manager.
- Include these details in the request:
  - the quota name
  - your current value and the value you need
  - the model ID and Region
  - your use case
  - projected steady and peak TPM and RPM, plus average input and output tokens per request
- AWS prioritizes customers who are already consuming their existing quota. A request can be denied if your traffic doesn't use it. New accounts also often start with lower quotas.

**3. Mitigate while you wait**
- Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter. The SDK's adaptive retry mode does this.
- Set `max_tokens` close to what you actually need. Bedrock reserves the full `max_tokens` against your TPM quota up front, so an oversized value causes throttling even when responses are short.
- Spread load across Regions with cross-Region inference profiles.
- For steady, predictable load, consider Provisioned Throughput. Reserved Tier is also an option for models that support it, and you request it through your account team.

If you tell me the model ID, Region and account that are throttling, I can check the exact quota and its current value. I can also look at the `InvocationThrottles` and token metrics in CloudWatch to see how far over the limit you are. If you'd like me to find out why the throttling started, I can open an Investigation.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
